priorities.name: Private space for confidential conversations and calls
priorities.issue: Associates routinely can't find a private room for confidential conversations because booths and phone rooms are all in use, and call noise carries across the floor.
whatItLooksLike: My role involves working with associates and their confidential information. Going to the office makes it very hard to be able to work productively while managing confidential information.
Lack of white noise to drown out others that work on the phone.

evidence.text: Focused / Private Work is the #1 priority category (88/100).
Privacy & Confidentiality: 39 people (22% of respondents), 57 comments, 72% negative; Noise & Distraction: 38 people (21% of respondents), 47 comments, 72% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Assess booth/phone-room capacity and booking against peak demand; test occupancy indicators and time limits before adding enclosed space.
priorities.siteMustDo: Track booth/phone-room demand-vs-availability for two weeks and escalate a sized capacity gap to Workplace Solutions.

priorities.name: Desk reservation clarity and workstation setup
priorities.issue: Associates can't see when a reserved room/desk will free up, and workstations are often left disassembled, costing setup time.
whatItLooksLike: Other associates being in a room that I have reserved for a meeting and me being unable to see when they are scheduled to be out of that capsule room, if they intend to leave at all.
Many times the workspace has been disassembled and requires that I figure out how to reconnect all pieces (monitors, keyboard, mouse). It's not as easy as just plugging in my laptop.

evidence.text: Desk Availability & Reservations: 29 people (16% of respondents), 36 comments, 56% negative — the 5th most-raised theme by people (it was the highest-volume theme before the November 2026 re-tag).

priorities.proposedAction: Review room/desk booking visibility (when a space frees up) and set a standard for how a workstation should be left.
priorities.siteMustDo: Confirm whether the booking tool surfaces end-times; test a 'leave it as you found it' workstation standard.

priorities.name: Workstation hardware reliability
priorities.issue: Reconnecting monitors/keyboard/mouse at shared desks is not plug-and-play, and connectivity is a frequent, highly negative complaint.
whatItLooksLike: Many times the workspace has been disassembled and requires that I figure out how to reconnect all pieces (monitors, keyboard, mouse). It's not as easy as just plugging in my laptop.

evidence.text: Hardware: 47 people (27% of respondents), 64 comments, 61% negative. Connectivity: 26 people (15% of respondents), 29 comments, 69% negative.

priorities.proposedAction: Standardize the dock/monitor setup and run routine equipment checks; validate connectivity in weak spots and route to Technology.
priorities.siteMustDo: Inspect workstations, standardize the setup, and log connectivity dead spots for Technology.

priorities.name: Thermal comfort (temperature)
priorities.issue: The office runs cold much of the time — associates mention space heaters — while others report it running hot, which points to uneven zoning rather than a single set-point.
whatItLooksLike: It is generally freezing in the Tampa office.
There were times when space heaters need to be used in the Tampa office and it was still cold.
The building gets very hot, this causes me to become uncomfortable and makes it hard to focus on work.

evidence.text: Temperature / Thermal: 24 people (14% of respondents), 27 comments, 74% negative.
Thermal / temperature comfort: Under Supported — friction 21/100 (43% under-supported).

priorities.proposedAction: Have Workplace Operations map hot and cold zones by time of day and check HVAC zoning, set-points and balancing; confirm whether personal heaters are being used to compensate.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log hot/cold zones and times for two weeks, submit them to building operations, and verify each correction holds.

priorities.name: Faster IT issue resolution on site
priorities.issue: When a connection or piece of equipment fails, associates say there is no on-site IT help and the only route is phone or chat, so small problems (a missing HDMI cable) cost large parts of the day. P3 covers the equipment itself; this covers how fast problems get fixed.
whatItLooksLike: There is not IT support at the office should I experience issues. The only resolution is to contact IT via phone or chat.

on several occasions I have been unable to connect and there is no IT support onsite to assist which results in large amounts of lost productivity being on the phone with IT support when there isn't even an HDMI cable available to plug into and no one to ask.

evidence.text: 'Technical issues are resolved in a timely manner' agreement: 3.53 vs 3.81 company average (Moderate) — just above the 3.5 'Needs attention' line.
Support / Help Services: 7 people (4% of respondents), 9 comments, 56% negative.
The survey's 'help resolving issues while on site' item has no Tampa scores, consistent with comments that there is no on-site IT support — confirm the site's support model.

priorities.proposedAction: Have Technology confirm Tampa's support model and pilot scheduled on-site tech hours plus a stocked spares kit (HDMI/USB-C cables, docks, keyboards, mice) at reception.
priorities.siteMustDo: Log every IT issue at the site — what failed and how long it took to fix — for 30 days, and use it to size on-site coverage with Technology.
